sentences.text: Appalachiosaurus was a bipedal predator belonging to the Eutyrannosauria clade, a group of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaurs closely related to true tyrannosaurids like Tyrannosaurus.
While early reconstructions suggested the animal possessed long arms with three large fingers, current understanding indicates it had much shorter arms with only two fingers.
The only known specimen is a juvenile measuring approximately 6.5 meters long and weighing 623 kilograms, suggesting adults were significantly larger.
Open sutures between skull bones confirm that this specific individual was definitely a juvenile.
Two fused tail vertebrae in the specimen may be the result of new bone growth following a minor or traumatic injury.
The type specimen was discovered by Auburn University geologist David King in July 1982, and the genus and species were formally named in 2005 by paleontologists Thomas Carr and Thomas Williamson.
The only known species, A. montgomeriensis, is named after Montgomery County, Alabama.
Although several bones of the specimen are crushed, it remains informative and displays unique characteristics.
In the original analysis, Asian tyrannosaurs like Alioramus and Alectrosaurus, as well as Eotyrannus from England, were excluded from the classification.
